transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Sarah Kim (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Horizon Head of Platform), Ethan Liu (Horizon Director of MLOps), Priya Nair (Horizon Security)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdown. Customer wants to validate cost model and look at per-route SLOs and routing policies. Asked about VPC/private options and SOC2/compliance.

Topics: usage analytics overview, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown by model & route, KV cache and prefix caching effects, dedicated vs hosted economics, data residency / KMS, next steps for pilot

Transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, I'm Sarah from Redwood, this is Liam our SE. We'll do a quick walkthrough of the Redwood Console usage analytics and then dig into per-route cost breakdowns.
[00:18] Maya Torres: great, thanks. We have about 30 minutes, want to see where cost is hiding in our current setup and if we can get better routing.
[00:27] Liam Patel: cool. Quick agenda slide \u2014 console -> usage analytics -> per route dashboards -> cost model -> q&a. I'll share my screen, lemme know if the screen share doesn't come through.
[00:40] Priya Nair: screen is good. also, real quick, we are very sensitive to SOC2 and KMS questions so we'll ask as we go.
[00:48] Liam Patel: totally, we'll call out where the security docs live and the VPC/private options.
[01:05] Liam Patel: okay opening the Console, top-left is the usage tab. By default you get token-level cost and latency histograms across routes, you can group by model, route, team, or tag. Note: sometimes the auto transcription says 'Consooole' but it's the console.
[01:30] Ethan Liu: nice, do you show embeddings cost separately? We run a lot of embeddings for search.
[01:36] Liam Patel: yep, embeddings show as a separate card. We break out generation tokens vs embedding units, and you can pivot by route or by model variant. Here's a sample from a demo tenant \u2014 you can see a spike in embedding qps around 10/31.
[02:05] Sarah Kim: one thing customers like is the per-route unit economics table \u2014 it shows avg tokens per request, average latency, model used, and a cost per 1k requests estimate. That lets you decide, hey, move this route to a quantized variant or enable prefix cache.
[02:28] Maya Torres: can you explain prefix cache effect again? we have a lot of similar prompts.
[02:33] Liam Patel: yeah so prefix (KV) caching stores repeated prefixes in the KV cache across requests \u2014 it reduces generation tokens and latency. In the console we surface a "cache hit" metric per route. In this example enabling cache dropped token spend by about 28% on a text-summary route.
[03:02] Ethan Liu: is that automatic or do we need to instrument code?
[03:07] Liam Patel: it's automatic on the runtime side if requests are similar and the route is pinning the same model variant. You can tune TTL and shard keys via the route config.
[03:25] Maya Torres: ok, what about dedicated capacity vs hosted for cost \u2014 we have spiky holiday traffic so predictability matters.
[03:33] Sarah Kim: for spike-heavy workloads Dedicated can be cheaper if you commit monthly, but for variable workloads hosted with burst can be simpler. We showed a quick cost comparison earlier \u2014 for Horizon's numbers we estimated dedicated would bust even after quantization at sustained 250 qps, but hosted made sense for the first pilot.
[04:05] Priya Nair: and data residency? some of our PII stays in region, can Redwood support VPC and customer-managed KMS?
[04:13] Liam Patel: yes \u2014 Private deployments support VPC and on-prem-like setups and you can bring your own KMS/HSM keys. For hosted we support per-tenant encryption and we have a KMS integration; we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs after the call.
[04:36] Maya Torres: perfect. show the per-route dashboard please.
[04:40] Liam Patel: switching to per-route view \u2014 each row is a route, you see call volume, avg tokens in/out, avg latency p50/p95, model, and estimated cost. You can click into a route for a time-series of token cost and latency and the granular segments.
[05:02] Liam Patel: note the model variants; you can set a fallback policy so if the fast low-cost variant is saturated it falls back to a higher-capacity variant automatically.
[05:20] Ethan Liu: do you show cost by model version? we run multiple versions in prod.
[05:24] Liam Patel: yes, versioning is first-class \u2014 cost and performance broken out by model version. You can also pin a route to a version for rollouts.
[05:40] Maya Torres: any noise in the console data, like sampling?
[05:44] Liam Patel: good q \u2014 we sample traces for deep debugging but usage/ billing metrics are full-coverage for token accounting. Tracing has sampling knobs.
[06:00] Sarah Kim: if it's helpful we can export a CSV of per-route cost and traffic so you can run your own finance model.
[06:08] Maya Torres: yes please send that.
[06:12] Liam Patel: noted. Export button is in the top-right.
[06:20] Maya Torres: what about embeddings cost, do you combine embeddings and generation for route grouping?
[06:24] Liam Patel: you can group by route so embeddings-heavy routes will show an embeddings card; also there's a consolidated view that aggregates all token-equivalent units across models.
[06:45] Ethan Liu: we're also concerned with latency SLOs \u2014 how do you show tail latency?
[06:50] Liam Patel: p50/p90/p95 are right there per route. And you can correlate latency with model, sequence length, and batching policy. There's an insights tab that suggests batch size changes or recommend quantization for high-cost routes.
[07:12] Maya Torres: you mentioned optimize features? can you run a rule that suggests quantization profiles?
[07:18] Liam Patel: Redwood Optimize runs offline analyses on your traces and suggests quantization and batching settings per model and route; it also estimates the impact on latency and quality. We'll share a sample Optimize report.
[07:35] Priya Nair: any impact on output quality when quantizing? we are sensitive for customer-facing responses.
[07:41] Liam Patel: yes that's part of the Optimize report \u2014 we run evals on your prompt set and show quality delta. Usually int8 quantization is low impact for many models, but we show regression alerts.
[07:58] Maya Torres: ok can you show an example cost breakdown per model?
[08:03] Liam Patel: sure \u2014 expanding the cost card: model, avg tokens, token unit cost, total tokens, total cost estimate. Here's an example: model Redwood-3-XL (quantized) cost per 1k tokens $X, vs full fp32 variant $Y. The console uses your configured pricing (or our hosted default) to compute estimates.
[08:35] Ethan Liu: can we plug in our negotiated prices?
[08:38] Sarah Kim: yes for Dedicated/Enterprise we can configure custom pricing in the console so the units reflect your committed rates.
[08:47] Maya Torres: we're planning an initial 8-week pilot, mostly hosted, then evaluate Dedicated before peak season. Does that timeline fit?
[08:56] Sarah Kim: that's a common path. Pilot -> pilot benchmark -> decision for dedicated during Q4 holiday window. We'll help with the benchmarking and a cost model.
[09:10] Liam Patel: walking through drilldown \u2014 here's a route with poor token efficiency, lots of repeated system prompts. We can show a suggested restructure, or enable prefix caching. Also you can set per-route routing policy: prefer low-cost model unless p95 latency > Xms where you failover to a higher perf variant.
[09:42] Ethan Liu: are these routing policies editable in the console?
[09:45] Liam Patel: yes they're on the route config page. You can set SLO thresholds, fallback sequence, model pools (dedicated vs hosted), and tagging.
[10:02] Maya Torres: curious about the latency vs cost graphs during bursts \u2014 can the console simulate peak usage?
[10:08] Liam Patel: we don't do synthetic sim in the console today, but our SE team can run a bench harness with your traffic trace to show latency/cost under load. We'll include that as part of the pilot.
[10:28] Priya Nair: security \u2014 who has access to these dashboards? RBAC?
[10:33] Sarah Kim: RBAC is supported \u2014 teams, roles, and token scoping. Audit logs are available and we surface admin-level exportable audit history. We'll send the admin RBAC matrix.
[10:50] Maya Torres: ok good. Also request retention \u2014 how long is the usage data kept?
[10:55] Liam Patel: default console usage retention is 13 months on hosted; we have longer retention as an add-on. For Private you control retention.
[11:10] Ethan Liu: there's a note about KV cache and PII \u2014 anything to be aware of?
[11:15] Liam Patel: KV cache is in memory in the serving runtime; for Private or Dedicated you can isolate and configure retention. For hosted we provide controls and we scrub data by default, but we'll confirm specifics in the security docs.
[11:36] Maya Torres: can you show a sample pilot workbook?
[11:40] Sarah Kim: yes, we have a pilot workbook that outlines objectives, traffic patterns, success criteria (cost delta, latency SLO, quality thresholds), and deliverables. We'll attach it.
[11:55] Liam Patel: jumping back to cost optimization \u2014 you can tag routes by product team and then get team-level billing so finance can allocate costs.
[12:06] Maya Torres: that would help for chargeback.
[12:09] Ethan Liu: how do we validate quality after quantization?
[12:13] Liam Patel: Optimize runs prompt-level evals and shows metrics like BLEU/ROUGE or LLM-specific quality scores on your golden prompts. You can opt into manual review if a regression is flagged.
[12:32] Priya Nair: ok, tiny nit \u2014 in the demo you mentioned "fallback to variant" \u2014 is that automatic? Does it require additional infra?
[12:39] Liam Patel: it's built into our routing layer \u2014 no extra infra for you, you just configure policies. For Dedicated you point routes to dedicated model pools.
[12:56] Maya Torres: if we were to pilot, what's the minimal data we need to provide?
[13:01] Liam Patel: 7 days of per-route traffic (CSV with route name, timestamp, tokens in/out, qps), your SLOs, and a prompt set for quality evals. That should be enough to run a representative bench.
[13:18] Ethan Liu: ok we'll extract that.
[13:22] Sarah Kim: timeline wise, we'll send the pricing worksheet and security pack by Thursday, and Liam will follow up on the bench plan.
[13:31] Priya Nair: one more question on encryption: for hosted, can we use our KMS for keys?
[13:37] Sarah Kim: hosted supports tenant-level encryption; for full BYOK you'll want Private/Dedicated with a KMS integration \u2014 we'll detail options in the doc.
[13:50] Maya Torres: great. Any final notes?
[13:54] Liam Patel: I'll add a sample per-route CSV export and a sample Optimize report to the follow-up email.
[14:05] Sarah Kim: recap of next steps: send price worksheet, security docs, Horizon sends traffic CSV, schedule pilot bench.
[14:15] Maya Torres: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[14:18] Ethan Liu: thanks, talk soon.
[14:20] Priya Nair: thanks.
